 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Showbiz Showbiz Filipiñana's lead actress Jorrybell Agoto passes away 
 By JANET SUSAN R. NEPALES Published November 19, 2026 4:57pm 
 Updated November 19, 2026 5:12pm + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Photo: Kamil Lipnica/FB Jorrybell Agoto, the lead actress of the Rafael Manuel-helmed film, " Filipiñana ," has passed away. She was 31.
 The unfortunate news was confirmed by Agoto's brother Jed, who told GMA News Online she died on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:20pm. "Yes po. My sister passed away na po," Jed said.
 Agoto, who was battling lymphoma, had been hospitalized and was in critical care. Her family had publicly appealed for financial assistance to help cover her mounting medical expenses.
 Speaking to GMA News Online, director-writer-producer Rafael Manuel said, “The tragedy of this loss cannot be put into words. The world has just lost one of its brightest stars. We have just lost a great friend. But our thoughts and prayers go out especially to Jorrybell’s family who have just lost a loving ate and a devoted daughter.”
 Producers Bianca Balbuena and Bradley Liew said, “We are devastated by this news. Not only is she the face of 'Filipiñana' but more than that, she is our friend, our sister, our beloved Jorrybell, ever so funny and kind, sweet and loving. We love her."
 They added, "We will always remember her and continue to keep her in our prayers. She can now rest without pain.”
 Agoto, who played Isabel, a 17-year-old golf course worker, in Manuel's debut feature film, was selected in 2025 to participate in the Berlinale Talents development programme.
 Oscar-winning director Sean Baker, who moderated the Los Angeles screening of the movie, in our earlier interview with him, pointed out that Agoto, who plays Isabel, has “depth in that performance that comes from very little dialogue. So, it has to be all expression. And so, strength comes through in that. I'm very impressed by her work.”
 Manuel told us in an earlier exclusive interview, “Jorrybell and I worked together ever since the short film, and I think she was still very green. It was one of the first short films she's ever made. And so, it was really a pleasure to grow with her over the seven years and really to grow the character with her over the seven years.”
 During the LA screening, Agoto was at the ICU in St. Luke’s Hospital in the Philippines. — LA, GMA News
